items.question: Which observances and which sixteenfold set are located in the principle of the person?
premises: Service, purity, contentment, and straightness are among the ten declared qualities.
These ten are located in the principle of the person.
A sixteenfold set ending with smell is also situated there.
items.inference: The principle of the person contains both the ten declared observances and a sixteenfold set extending to smell.
uncertainties: The full list of all ten qualities is not explicit in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: In the principle of the person are the ten declared qualities, including service, purity, contentment, and straightness. There too is situated a sixteenfold set ending with smell.

items.question: What bonds and principles arise from the world called the body-bond upward?
premises: Beginning from the world called the body-bond, the qualities of intellect come next.
In that same domain the ego appears as eightfold and in three ways.
Bonds beginning with desire also arise there.
items.inference: Above the body-bond world unfold intellect, a differentiated ego, and desire-based bonds.
uncertainties: The exact referent of the eightfold and threefold divisions is compressed in the verse.
items.plain_english: Starting from the world called the body-bond, the qualities of intellect appear. There the ego is present in eightfold and threefold forms, along with bonds beginning with desire.

items.question: How are the bonds in the person classified and what effect do they have?
premises: The bonds are divided into adventitious, Ganesha-related, and Vidyeshvara-related types.
These three kinds are situated in the person.
They obstruct the path to liberation.
items.inference: Three classes of bonds present in the person function as obstacles to liberation.
uncertainties: The precise doctrinal scope of the Ganesha and Vidyeshvara divisions is not spelled out here.
items.plain_english: The bonds are threefold: adventitious, of the Ganeshas, and of the Vidyeshvaras. They are present in the person and block the path to liberation.

items.question: What is defined as a bond in relation to supreme Shiva?
premises: Supreme Shiva is characterized as nondual consciousness, freedom, and beauty.
Anything other than that supreme described form is distinguished from it.
Such otherness is called a bond.
items.inference: A bond is whatever falls away from the supreme nondual freedom of Shiva.
items.plain_english: Whatever is other than the supreme Shiva, whose nature is nondual consciousness, freedom, and beauty, is called a bond.

items.question: Why do persons arise even when the supreme Lord remains full?
premises: The supreme Lord remains full even when personhood is assumed.
In that state there is non-recognition of his own nature.
This non-recognition is described as wondrous.
items.inference: Personhood arises through a wondrous non-recognition of the Lord's own full nature.
items.plain_english: Thus, even though the supreme Lord remains full, when personhood is assumed there arises a wondrous non-recognition of his own nature; from that come persons.

items.question: How does one become free from all the bonds present in the person?
premises: There are bonds both stated and unstated, described in the Paratantra.
All these bonds are present in the person.
By purifying them there, one is released from becoming.
items.inference: Liberation from becoming comes through purifying all bonds present in the person.
uncertainties: The specific method of purification is not detailed in this verse.
items.plain_english: All the bonds, whether stated or unstated and described in the Paratantra, are present in the person. By purifying them there, one is freed from worldly becoming.

items.question: Which divine beings inhabit the levels above the person in niyati and time?
premises: Above the person, in niyati, there are ten Shankaras.
Those Shankaras are described as golden-colored and very white.
In the principle of time there are ten Shivas.
items.inference: The levels above the person are inhabited by ten Shankaras in niyati and ten Shivas in time.
uncertainties: The verse gives appearance details for the Shankaras but not for the Shivas.
items.plain_english: Above the person, in niyati, dwell ten Shankaras, golden and very white. In the principle of time dwell ten Shivas.

items.question: What world and retinue are found in the principle of raga?
premises: In raga there is the world of Viresha.
Each has ten million and sixteen thousand attendants.
It is a city of teachers and students.
items.inference: The raga level contains Viresha's world populated by vast retinues and by teachers with students.
uncertainties: It is slightly ambiguous whether the large number applies to each principal figure or to the world as a whole.
items.plain_english: In raga is the world of Viresha, a city of teachers and students, with ten million and sixteen thousand attendants for each.

items.question: What powers illuminate the world in impure knowledge?
premises: In impure knowledge there is a world radiant with nine Shaktis.
These Shaktis extend up to Manonmani.
They are declared to begin with Vama.
items.inference: The world of impure knowledge is defined by a ninefold Shakti group from Vama to Manonmani.
items.plain_english: In impure knowledge there is a world shining with nine Shaktis, beginning with Vama and extending up to Manonmani.

items.question: What worlds are described in kala and in the transition to maya?
premises: In kala there is the supreme world of the triad of great gods.
Beyond that comes maya.
Maya is described as threefold and chiefly filled with endless ten-millions.
items.inference: Kala contains the supreme world of three great gods, and above it maya opens as a vast threefold domain.
uncertainties: The referent of the endless ten-millions is not explicitly named in this verse.
items.plain_english: In kala is the supreme world of the three great gods. Beyond that is maya, a threefold domain filled chiefly with countless millions.

items.question: How is maya structured and what group of deities is associated with it in the Shaiva scripture?
premises: Maya is pervaded by cavities called bhaga.
This teaching is given in the Shaiva scripture.
A group of eight great gods extends to the measure of a thumb at night.
items.inference: Maya is described as a cavity-filled domain associated with eight great gods in Shaiva teaching.
uncertainties: The phrase about the thumb-measure and night is terse and may have a technical ritual-cosmological sense.
items.plain_english: That maya is pervaded by cavities called bhaga, as taught in the Shaiva scripture. Again, there is a group of eight great gods extending to the measure of a thumb at night.

items.question: How are the Vama and other powers described across different scriptural teachings?
premises: The powers beginning with Vama rule over the eight circles.
In the teaching of Shrimalini they are described in that role.
In the earlier sacred teaching they are said to begin from the level of the person.
items.inference: The same Vama-led powers are correlated across teachings with both cosmic rulership and placement from the person upward.
uncertainties: The exact mapping between the two scriptural presentations is compressed.
items.plain_english: Likewise, in the teaching of Shrimalini, the powers beginning with Vama are described as ruling the eight circles; in the earlier sacred teaching they are said to begin from the level of the person.

items.question: Who are said to dwell in the principle of maya according to the Shaiva scripture?
premises: The Shaiva scripture places these beings in the principle of maya.
They are associated with Ananta.
They include skull-vow observers, self-offerers, and harsh ascetics.
items.inference: The maya level is inhabited by severe ascetic groups under the Shaiva account linked to Ananta.
items.plain_english: In the Shaiva scripture they are placed in the principle of maya, under Ananta: skull-vow observers, those who offer their own limbs, and practitioners of harsh austerities.

items.question: How do the ascetics progress through the principles and where do they arrive?
premises: These ascetics are fearless and observe the sword-edge vow.
They know the principles.
They gradually reach each principle up to where the lord is called Ananta.
items.inference: Through disciplined ascent they move principle by principle until reaching Ananta's domain.
items.plain_english: Fearless and observing the sword-edge vow, knowing the principles, they gradually ascend through each principle until they reach the place where the lord is called Ananta.

items.question: What is said about the abode beyond Ananta's lordship?
premises: A higher abode is said to exist beyond that lord.
The deity there performs maintenance, dissolution, and creation.
That deity guards the door of the cave and the bhaga.
items.inference: Beyond Ananta is a higher divine station governing cosmic functions and guarding the threshold of the cave.
uncertainties: The syntax is compressed and reads like a citation fragment.
items.plain_english: And it is said that beyond him is the abode of the lord of Ananta, the god who performs creation, maintenance, and dissolution, and who guards the door of the cave and the bhaga.

items.question: What does the lord bestow on persons from the cavity of maya?
premises: From the cavity of maya he draws things out repeatedly.
He bestows merits, powers such as smallness, knowledges, austerities, pleasures, and yogic attainments.
These gifts are given to persons.
items.inference: The lord distributes a wide range of attainments to persons by drawing them out from maya's cavity.
items.plain_english: Drawing them out again and again from the cavity of maya, he bestows on persons merits, powers such as minuteness, knowledges, austerities, pleasures, and yogic attainments.

items.question: How do Ananta and the other lords shine in their office within the cave?
premises: Their strength is kindled by his power.
They function like lamps dispelling darkness in the office of the cave.
All from Ananta onward to those beginning with Shatabhava shine in this way.
items.inference: The subordinate lords shine by borrowed divine power while administering the cave domain.
uncertainties: The exact identity of the group ending with Shatabhava is not specified here.
items.plain_english: Empowered by his energy, all the lords from Ananta onward, down to those beginning with Shatabhava, shine like lamps dispelling darkness in the office of the cave.

items.question: Why does Shiva preside over the unmanifest and bring forth the world?
premises: Shiva presides over the unmanifest.
He brings forth the world by the command of Shambhu.
He is the cause of authority over the pure and impure streams.
items.inference: Shiva's cosmic activity over the unmanifest is grounded in delegated authority over both pure and impure streams.
items.plain_english: Presiding over the unmanifest, Shiva brings forth the world by the command of Shambhu, because he is the cause of authority over both the pure and impure streams.

items.question: What role do those established in the great station of Shiva's qualities perform?
premises: Some beings are established in that great station connected with Shiva's qualities.
They are first among those beginning with Ananta.
They perform creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the world.
items.inference: Beings established in Shiva's qualities exercise delegated cosmic governance beginning with Ananta.
items.plain_english: Those first established in that great station endowed with Shiva's qualities, beginning with Ananta, become the agents of the world's creation, maintenance, and dissolution.

items.question: What lies beyond the cavity of maya and how does it function as the world's womb?
premises: The cavity of maya has already been described.
Beyond it is the cave, called the womb of the world.
Its generative activity occurs as the stirring of the lord's power takes effect among them.
items.inference: Beyond maya's cavity, the cave functions as the generative womb activated by the lord's power.
uncertainties: The referent of 'among them' is not explicit in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: This has been called the cavity of maya. Beyond it is the cave, the womb of the world, where generation occurs as the stirring of the lord's power takes effect.

items.question: What happens when the lord desires the goddess within the womb-openings called bhaga?
premises: There are womb-openings rich with various desires.
These are called bhaga.
When the lord desires the goddess who follows his will, a generative condition is set.
items.inference: The lord's desire for the consenting goddess within the bhaga-openings initiates manifestation.
items.plain_english: In the womb-openings, rich with various desires and called bhaga, when the lord desires the goddess who follows his will, the generative process begins.

items.question: What offspring arise in each bhaga and how fully are they described?
premises: In each bhaga, offspring beginning with the unmanifest are born.
These offspring are extremely subtle.
Their nature is not described in the prescribed texts.
items.inference: Each bhaga generates extremely subtle offspring from the unmanifest onward, beyond full scriptural description.
items.plain_english: In each bhaga, offspring beginning with the unmanifest are born from her. They are so extremely subtle that their nature is not described in the prescribed texts.

items.question: How are the many womb-cavities within maya illustrated by analogy?
premises: Many inner rooms can be enclosed within one hall.
The womb-cavities exist within one head-hall of maya.
The verse compares the two structures directly.
items.inference: The many womb-cavities of maya are arranged like many enclosed rooms within a single hall.
uncertainties: The term 'head-hall of maya' is metaphorical and not further explained here.
items.plain_english: Just as many enclosed inner rooms can exist within one hall, so many womb-cavities exist within the single head-hall of maya.

items.question: How do the Rudras dwell within the many cavities of maya?
premises: The cavities are covered by subtle layers and walls of maya.
Because of this covering, they are invisible to one another.
Countless happy Rudras dwell in each cavity.
items.inference: Maya partitions its cavities so that innumerable Rudras dwell separately and happily within them.
items.plain_english: Covered by subtle layers and walls of maya, invisible to one another, countless happy Rudras dwell there in each cavity.
